proof_scope: A cutoff Riesz decomposition gives finite-p disc norms controlled by a finite negative center; Tonelli in coordinate variables and a selected center give local Lp/L1 estimates and all-finite-p convergence. Fixed smooth background and normalized compactness give uniform global Lp norms. For a positive-mass model in a big class, residual measure domination mu_u<=nu+a mu_phi, a<1, and superlinear capacity domination imply bounded relative type, with an explicit moment-depth constant. Full-mass sublevel tails and comparison precede a geometric finite-extinction iteration; relative domination upgrades the measure conclusion pointwise. Energy sublevels and Lp densities with the explicitly retained capacity hypothesis give quantitative corollaries.
